title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nasdaq tumbled 1.3% Thursday (worst day since August) and S&P 500 fell 0.5% as AI-linked optics names (Coherent, Corning, Lumentum) each dropped >5%; Dow eked out a 0.1% gain.

Markets: Treasury yields eased further after a well-received 30-year auction (10Y ~5.23%, 30Y ~5.61%); Brent crude jumped over $4 to $104.28 — its highest since September — on Gulf of Mexico production shutdowns ahead of Hurricane Isaias.
Markets: This follows record closes earlier in the week, with the S&P 500 topping 7,800 and the Nasdaq above 27,400 for the first time.
Companies: Chipotle surged more than 6% on a report Starbucks explored a takeover; Starbucks said it remains "laser-focused" on its own strategy.
Companies: PepsiCo cut its full-year outlook citing consumer pressure, but shares rose nearly 4% as investors welcomed the CEO's focus on fixing the soft-drinks business.
Companies: Microsoft and Nvidia launched the Surface Ultra AI PC ($2,599, RTX Spark chip), pushing further into on-device AI computing.
Macro/Policy: All eyes are on the Fed's October 28 decision after September's hike to 3.75%-4.00%; a cooler September jobs report has pared back bets on another hike this month.
Macro/Policy: Three fired OpenAI researchers wrote to the company's board urging it to preserve outside visibility into AI reasoning, amid a wider debate over AI safety oversight.
